claims.text: As-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi films or ribbons exhibit an ordered single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloys have inherent compositional inhomogeneity.
The as-deposited alloys undergo a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition.
The as-deposited transition produces a large but hysteretic magnetocaloric entropy change.
A controlled low-temperature anneal near 400°C promotes localized atomic rearrangements and increases chemical short-range order.
Suitable annealing can enhance chemical short-range order without significant grain growth or phase separation.
Increased chemical short-range order minimizes local strain fields.
Increased chemical short-range order reduces interfacial-energy variations between coexisting magnetic and crystallographic phases.
Reduced strain and interfacial-energy variation lower the nucleation-energy barrier for the emerging phase.
Lower nucleation barriers produce a more diffuse and broadened phase transformation.
Annealing-induced chemical ordering lowers domain pinning.
A broadened phase transformation and lower domain pinning reduce transition hysteresis.
Annealed samples will have a broader magnetocaloric transition profile than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have a smaller hysteresis width than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealing will make the magnetocaloric entropy change more gradual.
A more gradual entropy change could improve dynamic heat exchange during refrigeration cycles.
The as-deposited films or ribbons have a limited surface-to-volume ratio.
The predictions apply only while annealing remains below conditions that cause grain coarsening or phase decomposition.
Residual stress and minor compositional fluctuations may also influence the magnetocaloric response.
